plugin.decklink_io.advisory.missing_fram: Frames are being repeated on output “{flow}”: the source is not delivering a fresh frame every frame period. On air the picture still looks clean (mode “{mode}”) — which is exactly why this advisory exists. The exact count is in “missing_frames_repeated” on the card state.
plugin.decklink_io.advisory.profile_part: Card {model} was only PARTLY normalised: after {switches} switch(es) to {to}, {left} sub-device(s) are still not in the target profile — their connectors stay off and no cable will carry anything there.
plugin.decklink_io.advisory.profile_swit: The profile of card {model} was normalised at start-up ({from} → {to}) and {cut} connector(s) that were carrying a signal were cut for the duration of the switch. Without that switch, the connectors the profile keeps off could not be woken at all.
plugin.decklink_io.attente.redeploiement: Redeploying — the card has not taken this setting yet. The page shows what you asked for.
plugin.decklink_io.avert.inactives: Some connectors are TURNED OFF by the active profile: a cable plugged into one of them does nothing, and nothing on the chassis says so.
plugin.decklink_io.avert.ordre: The connector order is the one the card reports, starting from the PCI side. Nothing in the driver guarantees it matches the real socket order: check with a cable before relying on it.
plugin.decklink_io.avert.trop_de_sorties: {c} carries {n} outputs and only sustains {max}: beyond that, some outputs run permanently late and THEIR AUDIO IS DROPPED, with nothing in the counters to show it. This does not work yet — bring it back down to {max} on this card.
plugin.decklink_io.bandeau.cote_pci_aide: This end of the drawing is the PCI Express edge connector — the gold tab that plugs into the motherboard. It is the ONLY landmark that does not depend on how the server is built: rack, tower or inverted chassis, it does not move. The reference input is the first socket on that side.
plugin.decklink_io.conteneur.arrete: The container is STOPPED ({st}) and has been for {s} s; nothing will bring it back on its own.
plugin.decklink_io.conteneur.attente_pil: This container is WAITING FOR ITS DRIVER: it was deliberately not started, because the driver is missing on this node. It will start by itself when the node reboots with the driver installed — there is nothing to do here.
plugin.decklink_io.conteneur.cause_pilot: The cause is most likely the missing driver reported above: without it the capture binary finds no card and exits a few seconds after start-up.
plugin.decklink_io.conteneur.demarrage: Start requested — the container is coming back.
plugin.decklink_io.conteneur.inconnu: This container is no longer in the orchestrator's database: there is nothing left for this page to query.
plugin.decklink_io.conteneur.muet: The container is reported as started but has not answered for {s} s.
plugin.decklink_io.conteneur.public: This flow is unavailable: the container has not answered for {s} s.
plugin.decklink_io.conteneur.voulu_demar: It is nevertheless meant to be running: it stopped by itself.

plugin.decklink_io.editeur.audio_entree_: 16 channels publish TWO flows of 8: « …_audio » for channels 1-8 and « …_audio_2 » for channels 9-16.
plugin.decklink_io.editeur.audio_sortie_: The bus carries 8-channel flows: 16 channels are cabled as TWO flows, 1-8 and 9-16. With no second flow cabled, channels 9-16 stay silent — the Cables page then shows an empty 9-16 audio port.
plugin.decklink_io.erreur.redeploiement: Redeploying — the container is restarting, the display will come back in a few seconds.

plugin.decklink_io.note.plafond_sorties: {c} would carry {n} outputs: beyond {max} on a single card, some outputs run late and THEIR AUDIO IS DROPPED. This does not work yet.
plugin.decklink_io.pilote.aussi_reglages: This driver is installed on the machine itself, not inside this container — and without waiting for this container:
plugin.decklink_io.pilote.consequence: No card can be opened while it is missing: both lists on this page will stay empty and the container stops a few seconds after it is created, even though the cards are present on the PCI bus.
plugin.decklink_io.pilote.etape.reboot: Reboot the node — kernel modules are only loaded at the next boot (Settings → Nodes → “Reboot node”).
plugin.decklink_io.pilote.etape.relance: Nothing more to do: the container will start by itself at the next boot, once the driver is in place.
plugin.decklink_io.pilote.inconnu_conseq: This node's agent is too old to answer (0.28.0 or later is required), so the Desktop Video driver state cannot be read from here. If it is missing, this container cannot start at all: the kernel then exposes no device under /dev/blackmagic and the card stays invisible, even when present on the PCI bus.
plugin.decklink_io.pilote.lien_reglages: Settings → Nodes and hardware → Deployment → Nodes
plugin.decklink_io.pilote.ou_trouver: The Linux “Desktop Video” archive, from blackmagicdesign.com → Support → Capture and Playback. A product registration form opens: the “Download only” link at the bottom left is enough, no account is needed. Fetch it from a workstation and upload it here: the node may have no outbound access, and the install runs offline. Version in service on this fleet as of 2026-10-30: 16.4a1 (dell-1); anything newer is fine.

type.decklink_io.cfg.inputs.help: A list [{"persistent_id": <id>, "flow": "<name>"}]. The persistent_id comes from tools/probe; it is the ONLY accepted identity. After a profile switch, the same sub-device index designates a physically DIFFERENT connector: a flow identified by index starts capturing something else without a single counter flinching.

type.decklink_io.cfg.outputs.help: A list [{"persistent_id": <id>, "flow": "<flow to play out>", "mode": "1080p50"}]. The mode is EXPLICIT and has no default: the mode iterator returns NTSC SD first, so “the first supported one” lands on NTSC SD.
